Calibration requires a fitted surface, e.g., logistic or XGBoost models, to align with empirical distributions. Leverage indexing (swing) measures sensitivity to outcomes, enabling attribution of impact. WPA quantifies contribution per action, enforcing zero-sum constraints. Failure modes include model drift (e.g., scoring-era shift) and misalignment between exact and calibrated surfaces. Empirical diagnostics such as permutation decomposition isolate heterogeneity from sequential dependencies. The two-surface architecture resolves this tradeoff by maintaining exactness for attribution and calibration for reporting.
